notes: The record of the comparison HILLSHADE already sits at E4 on, written after the fact from artifacts committed at the time.

This is the weakest of the three legs and the record should say so. GDAL encodes the shared intensity as 1 + 254*h where this project writes 255*h, a fixed (1 - h) offset that consumes most of a one-level budget on its own, so the measured maximum difference of exactly 1.00 level is the encoding, not a shading error. What carries the claim is the other two legs: the unquantised intensity against the closed form differs by 0.0000643, and this project's intensity re-encoded in GDAL's own 1 + 254*h scale reproduces the reference exactly.

The reference was re-run on 2026-07-30 from the command in command.txt, with GDAL 3.13.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin/gdaldem, and reproduced hillshade-gdal.asc byte for byte. The original run recorded its version, platform and command but not its executable path; the path below is the one that reproduced the artifact.

reference.containerPinningNote: No container runtime was used for these references, so no image digest exists to record; the executable path, the reported version, the exact command line and the artifact's own sha256 stand in for it, and the reproduction on 2026-07-30 is what makes that substitution checkable.

datasets.description: The frozen analytic DEM, shared with the slope and aspect studies.
GDAL 3.13.1 single-direction hillshade on that DEM, azimuth 315, altitude 45, z-factor 1, the reference side of the comparison.

parameterSets.description: Single-direction Lambert relief from a Horn gradient, sun azimuth 315 clockwise from north, altitude 45 above the horizon, z-factor 1, one-cell border excluded, compared on the shipped 8-bit level.

statusReason: All 11,564 interior cells are within the preregistered one-level tolerance, with a maximum difference of exactly 1.00 level and an RMSE of 0.536; the maximum sits on the tolerance because the two byte encodings differ by up to one level, which is why the claim rests on the closed-form leg and the exact re-encoding identity as well as on this one.

unsupported: Byte-identical agreement under this project's own encoding. The two encodings differ by a fixed (1 - h) offset; the identity holds only after re-encoding into GDAL's 1 + 254*h scale.
Multidirectional relief, which is a different illumination model on each side and diverges by up to 50 of 255 levels; it coincides only at zero gradient.
Sun positions other than azimuth 315 and altitude 45, and z-factors other than 1.
The one-cell border, which the reference command leaves undefined.
The point-cloud-to-DTM pipeline. This study starts from a DEM.
Accuracy of any kind. Hillshade is a shading index, not a physical quantity, and this comparison carries no elevation-accuracy meaning.
